unreg:season_stat_feats.reviewer: reviewer-zblk-MLB (Claude agent, agent verification, not human expert)
unreg:season_stat_feats.rederivation_notes: My own chain before reading the record: eight unrelated any-player events. Six single-game feats (individual no-hitter, perfect game, 20-K game, 4-HR game, 2-grand-slam game, 500-ft Statcast HR) are rare-event unions over remaining team-games, each with its own sub-chain (starter length and exit hazard, K rate, contact/defence/scoring for no-hit bids; per-PA HR rate x 4+ PA for 4-HR; bases-loaded PA opportunity for grand slams; tail of tracked HR distance by park/altitude). Two are accumulation races (any pitcher 20 regular-season wins: wins to date, remaining starts, win credit; any hitter 50 HR and 50 SB: pace, PA, health). Required: feats-to-date ledger, games remaining, playoff exposure for the six that count playoffs, rotation and IL state. I re-listed KXMLBSTAT via the Kalshi API (11 events, eight non-velocity, wording matches the author's evidence file; markets opened 2026-06-27, W20/5050 closed 2026-09-28, others 2026-10-29; early_close_condition 'close and expire after the event occurs'). The record matches my chain on stages and regular-season-only scoping; it differs by hard-coding the unverified 'individual' no-hitter reading into the primary hazard, carrying stale 40-SB text, omitting the early-close term, and leaving team-season blueprint inputs unaudited.

findings.text: mlb.leaguewide_rare_game_event_hazard (primary) hard-codes the unverified 'individual' no-hitter reading: its rationale says only individual no-hitters count here and the measurement counts only games where one pitcher recorded all outs. The rule text is 'any pitcher records a no hitter'; the record's own sstat_rules_not_sampled says combined no-hitters are a title inference only. Combined no-hitters are a large share of recent no-hitters, so the required history and rate change. The input must compute both readings (individual and combined, nine-inning and shortened) as branches, as the streak record does for runs.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: hazard input now computes individual and combined no-hitter branches (nine-inning and shortened) with nested monotonicity; wording fixed in settlement, summary, s3, variants; gap sstat_no_hitter_definition added (verified zblk3).

findings.text: mlb.joint_season_hr_sb_distribution mechanism still says 'A 50 HR and 40 SB season' (stale; 40 SB is the separate KXMLBSTATCOUNT contract) while the event is 50 HR and 50 SB. The input is defined for one hitter; the contract is any hitter, and the union over candidate hitters is not written down (stage s5 and the interaction speak of a single hitter).
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: joint HR/SB input mechanism now says 50/50 here and 50/40 only for KXMLBSTATCOUNT, and the any-hitter union over reachable candidates is written into measurement, s5 and the joint interaction (verified zblk3).

findings.text: Contract facts from the Kalshi market object are missing: can_close_early true with 'This market will close and expire after the event occurs', W20 and 5050 close 2026-09-28 versus 2026-10-29 for the other six, and markets opened 2026-06-27 (mid-season). So the as-of feats-to-date ledger and games-remaining state are the real starting state, and no input or dataset names a feats-to-date ledger (only a mention in the hazard measurement).
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: early_close_condition and open/close times added to contract and evidence_zblk (match API fetch); mlb.season_feat_ledger_state added and staged in s1, s2 with dataset feeds (verified zblk3).

findings.text: Input overlap and mislabelled data wiring: the hazard input contains its own 500-ft GPD (threshold 450 ft) and bottom-up 4-HR/grand-slam cross-checks that duplicate hr_distance_tail_exceedance (threshold 440 ft) and bases_loaded_pa_opportunity, with no DUPLICATE audit; interactions 1 and 3 are covariates inside those inputs rather than interactions; the 'scoring rulings and Kalshi wording' dataset lists bracket_path_enumeration, rule_regime, hr_environment and contact_defense as fed by it, and no dataset supplies playoff-participation probabilities for the six playoff-counting events; nested monotonicity (perfect game within no-hitter) is not recorded.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: 500-ft GPD and bottom-up terms removed from the hazard (calibration cross-check only), interactions replaced, dataset feeds corrected, playoff-participation dataset and nested monotonicity added (verified zblk3).

findings.text: Blueprint season_stat is a team win-total blueprint; season_sim, preseason_projections, pythag_luck, remaining_sos, depth_injury_war and run_dist are inherited by this archetype but neither audited nor staged. rules_evidence cites a velocity event (26P107) that belongs to the other archetype, and the eight events' wording exists only in evidence_zblk, not in the sampled rules file.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: blueprint re-homed to leaders, all 27 effective inputs audited, rule_regime attached; KXMLBSTAT quote retained with an explicit note that only the velocity event is sampled (verified zblk3).

unreg:player_home_run_exposure.reviewer: reviewer-zblk-MLB (Claude agent, agent verification, not human expert)
unreg:player_home_run_exposure.rederivation_notes: My own chain before reading the record: a named hitter's HR count over (a) one playoff series (KXMLBSERIESHR, ladder rungs, count over a random number of games) or (b) a calendar window (KXMLBNEXTHR, one-or-more). Stages: exposure frame (series length from per-game win probabilities, or scheduled games with off days/doubleheaders), participation (round roster, start, platoon, injury absorbing state), plate appearances and pitchers faced (rotation order, bullpen, handedness), per-PA HR probability (power regressed, park, wind, temperature), game-shared overdispersion, aggregation (convex for 2+, saturating for 1+), settlement (official HR, inside-the-park, no start gate, missed-game treatment, whether All-Star Game or postseason falls in window). Required: schedule/bracket, lineup and IL feeds, Statcast, weather. The record matches this chain closely. It differs in a primary input definition that omits the HR probability, an unaddressed All-Star Game inside the sampled window, an asserted No-settlement for missed games, and a coaching-scheme N/A that contradicts its own pitch-around gap.

findings.text: mlb.window_exposure_schedule (primary engine for KXMLBNEXTHR) defines P(at least one) = 1 - prod_g(1 - p_g x P(healthy through g)) where p_g is participation only; there is no per-game HR probability, so as defined it is the probability of playing, not of homering. The audit calls it 'the right object' without noticing; only stage s5 text has the correct product. The definition also carries pitcher/two-way/reliever wording irrelevant to a hitter market. Fix the measurement to include participation x per-game HR probability.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: mlb.window_exposure_schedule now multiplies participation by per-game HR probability q_g from per-PA rate and expected PA in P(at least one) (verified zblk3).

findings.text: KXMLBNEXTHR sampled window (after May 26, before Aug 1, 2026) contains the All-Star Game and break; the sibling KXMLBSTATCOUNT rule explicitly excludes the All-Star Game but this text is silent, and boundary-date semantics (time zone, games on May 26/Aug 1) are not stated. Variants list postseason but not the All-Star Game.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: All-Star Game and boundary-date ambiguity added to variants and as gap hrx_window_boundaries; sibling KXMLBSTATCOUNT exclusion confirmed in sampled rules (verified zblk3).

findings.text: Summary says a missed series 'resolves No' as if stated; for KXMLBSERIESHR the text only counts total home runs (so No for 2+ is arithmetic) and void treatment is unaddressed, which the record's own hrx_missed_games_settlement concedes.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: summary and variants no longer assert that a missed series resolves No; void treatment declared in hrx_missed_games_settlement (verified zblk3; a NEXTHR rules_evidence line still overstates, reported separately).

findings.text: coaching_scheme is NOT_APPLICABLE ('no separate scheme input needed') while unresolved hrx_pitch_around_postseason says intentional walks and pitching around are unmodelled; mlb.playoff_games_pa_distribution is leader-market text whose measurement depends on bracket_path_enumeration, which this archetype does not carry; series_hr_exposure keeps crude 0.95/0.55 start constants; new_inputs copies use placeholder raw_data 'see catalog definition of ...'.

unreg:pitcher_scoreless_innings_streak.reviewer: reviewer-zblk-MLB (Claude agent, agent verification, not human expert)
unreg:pitcher_scoreless_innings_streak.rederivation_notes: My own chain before reading the record: reaching N scoreless innings is survival over 3N outs from a carried streak total, ended by the first run (under an all-runs or earned-runs reading, inherited runners charged to the starter). Needs: as-of ledger (outs banked since the stated start, alive flag), remaining regular-season starts (rotation, rest, skips, IL, clinch rest), outs per start (exit hazard, manager protection of a streak), per-inning scoreless probability by opponent, park, defence and HR/BB/K talent, luck regression for a pitcher selected on a streak, nested rungs settling on reach and No on break, regular-season end, partial innings at one third. Contract read from the sampled KXMLBSISTREAK text. The record matches this chain well and handles the run-definition ambiguity as a two-branch mixture. Differences: unsourced scoring-correction window, a data source that cannot expose charged runs, an arithmetic overstatement, and park/weather named in prose without an input.

findings.text: mlb.scoreless_streak_ledger_state and the dataset row assume a 48-hour official scoring-correction window and re-pull 'after the 48-hour window'; no source is given and it is not in the unresolved list. The ledger and play-by-play rows also name Baseball Savant as a source of earned/unearned and inherited-runner flags; Savant event data does not carry run-charging; MLB Stats API or Retrosheet would, and that is unverified here.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: unsourced 48-hour window and Savant run-charging source removed from the ledger input and dataset; gap sis_scoring_source_and_window declares the source and window unverified (verified zblk3).

findings.text: Nonlinearity text says moving q from 0.78 to 0.82 'nearly doubles' a ten-inning gap probability; (0.82/0.78)^10 is about 1.65. The summary also says average starters sit 'well below' 0.75-0.85 whereas league average per-inning scoreless is about 0.72-0.73.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: nonlinearity corrected to (0.82/0.78)^10 = 1.65x and the per-inning figures labelled modelling assumptions in the summary (verified zblk3).

findings.text: Stage s3 and the environment coverage claim park run environment but cite no park input (mlb.park and mlb.weather_pit are inherited from blueprint player_pitch, unstaged and unaudited); sp_workload and leash are also inherited via that blueprint and conflict with the sp_hook_hazard_curve exposure used here. The IL/role-change reading ('streak does not break from missing starts') is an inference placed in variants as if settled, although it is also declared unresolved.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: blueprint re-homed to pitcher_er, park, weather and HR vulnerability staged in s3, inherited inputs audited, IL reading worded as inference (verified zblk3).

unreg:pitch_velocity_extremes.reviewer: reviewer-zblk-MLB (Claude agent, agent verification, not human expert)
unreg:pitch_velocity_extremes.rederivation_notes: My own chain before reading the record: season max of tracked release speed is an extreme value over near-peak fastballs from a tiny pool of arms with a physical ceiling; needs candidate pool (tracked peaks, AAA/call-ups, foreign-league arms), exposure (role, appearances, postseason), situational lift (leverage, rest, temperature, pitch number), injury hazard, tracking source and calibration (Hawk-Eye release speed, park offsets, rounding, revisions, 107.0 vs 107), and window scope (spring, ASG). Contracts: KXMLBFASTPITCH named pitcher 107.0+, and KXMLBSTAT any-pitcher 105/106/107+ which I re-listed from the Kalshi API (105+ event has no market object; 106+ and 107+ finalized No; all close early on occurrence). Thresholds 105 and 106 lie at or near the tracked record (about 105.8) whereas 107 is beyond it, so the physical regime differs by event. The record matches the generic chain and cleanly removed the season-feat residue; it differs in calibrating inputs to 107 only, carrying unsourced record claims, and a feed-anomaly input with no obtainable history.

findings.text: Inputs and unresolved items are calibrated to 107 only while the archetype now owns three nested any-pitcher thresholds. mlb.max_velocity_extreme_distribution has p_i = P(speed >= 107.0) hard-coded; pool inclusion (3-season max >= 103), anomaly screens (>= 104) and the 'physical tail near zero so anomalies dominate' interaction assume the line is beyond every tracked pitch. For 105+ (and nearly 106+) the line is inside or at the observed record, so an empirical tail is estimable and the extrapolation and anomaly-dominance narrative does not apply. No input, interaction or unresolved entry treats the nested thresholds or the regime change by threshold.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: extreme-value, pool and anomaly inputs parametrised by threshold T in {105,106,107} with empirical versus extrapolated regimes, monotonicity, regime-switch interaction and gap velo_threshold_regimes (verified zblk3).

findings.text: Record claims are stated as fact without a source: fewer than a dozen pitchers above 104 mph per season, all-time tracked maxima near 105-106, 107 beyond every tracked pitch, and 'documented' park biases in radar systems (velo_park_offsets is declared unverified but the claim is also in the rationale). mlb.velocity_feed_anomaly_rate has no obtainable history (own-capture only, intermediate feed states unarchived) and there is no DATA_UNAVAILABLE unresolved entry; the summary suggests a feed glitch may be a likelier route to YES than the physical tail with no evidence any such published reading has occurred.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: unsourced record and park-bias claims marked recollection/SOURCE_UNVERIFIED throughout; feed-glitch route stated undocumented; DATA_UNAVAILABLE gap velo_feed_history added (verified zblk3).

findings.text: Audit of mlb.max_velocity_extreme_distribution says its 'exponential-tail fit' and independence overstate probability, but the catalog measurement is already a bounded GPD (xi < 0) with a park-offset sensitivity run; audit text and definition disagree. Omitted contract fact: Kalshi markets carry early_close_condition 'close and expire after the event occurs', which bears directly on the first-published-versus-corrected reading gap. Candidate pool sources omit NPB/KBO arms without Statcast history.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: max_velocity audit corrected (catalog was already a bounded GPD), early_close_condition added to settlement and anomaly text, NPB/KBO arms added to pool sources (verified zblk3).

findings.text: Blueprint season_stat (team win-total blueprint) is still inherited: season_sim, preseason_projections, pythag_luck, remaining_sos, depth_injury_war, run_dist are carried by a pitch-velocity archetype and are neither audited nor staged. rules_evidence has only KXMLBFASTPITCH; the any-pitcher wording is quoted only inside settlement_definition because KXMLBSTAT is filed under season_stat_feats.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: blueprint re-homed to player_pitch with all inherited inputs audited and KXMLBSTAT quote restored under event_routing (verified zblk3; inherited blueprint interactions reported separately).

unreg:player_and_team_counting_specials.reviewer: reviewer-zblk-MLB (Claude agent, agent verification, not human expert)
unreg:player_and_team_counting_specials.rederivation_notes: My own chain before reading the record: two league-wide postseason counts (KXMLBWALKOFFS at least 5 walk-offs, rule counts any walk-off; KXMLBPLAYOFFHRS at least 75 HR incl. inside-the-park). Each is observed-to-date plus a sum over remaining playoff games. Games remaining: bracket path, Wild Card bo3 (all at higher seed), Division bo5 (2-2-1), LCS/WS bo7 (2-3-2), per-game win probabilities, off days. Walk-offs: home team bats last only if tied or trailing after the top of the ninth (skipped bottoms), closer deployment, extras (postseason has no automatic runner), a run-scoring chain with walk-off stopping rule. HR: both lineups, pitchers, park factor, October weather, ball regime, game-shared overdispersion. No per-player element. The record matches this chain. It differs in input-set hygiene after the split: the archetype still inherits the player_hit blueprint's hitter-level inputs, two 'detached' inputs are still carried, stale audit text names a departed branch, and series-length inputs are best-of-seven only.

findings.text: The split is not effective at input-list level. The catalog entry keeps blueprint player_hit, whose 17 inputs (hitter_quality, hitter_contact_profile, platoon, batter_vs_pitch, sp_quality, bullpen_talent, lineup_pit, park, defense, babip_luck, contact_dist, rbi_opportunity, sb_context, bvp_history, expected_pa, weather_pit, ladder_structure) are inherited by a league-count archetype. mlb.expected_pa and mlb.lineup_pit are audited IRRELEVANT and logged as 'detached', but both are blueprint inputs and remain carried; 13 inherited hitter inputs are neither audited nor staged. The brief-level residue 'one input list that serves none fully' persists through the blueprint; the blueprint must be changed (patches cannot change blueprint).
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: blueprint changed from player_hit to extras, 15 hitter/pitcher inputs detached, effective list of 23 inputs fully audited, stale interactions dropped (verified zblk3).

findings.text: Exposure inputs cover only best-of-seven: mlb.series_length_distribution is labelled and measured for 4/5/6/7 games and bracket_path_enumeration cites a '2-3-2 or 2-2-1-1-1' home pattern (2-2-1-1-1 is not an MLB pattern), while Wild Card bo3 (all games at the higher seed) and Division bo5 (2-2-1) supply most playoff games; calibration history for the 12-team bo3 round is only a few seasons and unflagged. mlb.postseason_league_hr_count's measurement uses mlb.park_specific_xhr, which this archetype does not carry.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: series_length_distribution and bracket_path_enumeration cover bo3/bo5/bo7 with the invalid 2-2-1-1-1 pattern removed and the format table flagged; postseason HR count uses carried hr_environment; gap cs_round_format_history (verified zblk3).

findings.text: Stale text from the former mixed record: audit of mlb.joint_season_hr_sb_distribution says it is attached in 'the KXMLBSTAT branch of pitch_velocity_extremes' (it was moved to season_stat_feats); audit of mlb.leash cites sp_workload for the streak (the streak record uses sp_hook_hazard_curve); three re-homed pointer gaps (unr_streak_break_definition, unr_serieshr_missed_games, unr_streak_inputs) and unr_generic_stat_variants stay as unresolved entries although they concern other archetypes. 'About a third' for walk-off HRs share is an unsourced figure.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: stale audit text corrected, unsourced 'about a third' figure removed from the record, re-homed pointer gaps kept and verified to point at existing sis_/hrx_ gaps (verified zblk3).
